tools.name: minerva_cad_references
tools.description: List the foreign mesh files (glTF/GLB or STL placed by the .mcad mesh() primitive) currently mounted in a live CAD editor. LEAN BY DEFAULT: each reference's name, its status, its WORLD bounding box and how many nodes it holds — a listing that stays small on a board of forty-five nodes. detail="full" adds the path the source wrote, the resolved path, the composed 4x4 pose, both frames of every box, the bounding box of every node inside it, and the load statistics (triangle_count, bytes, load_ms, outlines_skipped); reference=<name> answers about one reference instead of all, and a name that is not mounted is an error naming the ones that are. Under detail="full" every box is millimetres in BOTH frames: 'local' is the reference's own converted frame — millimetres, Z-up, with the mesh() pose taken back off (the numbers to write back into the DSL; the file's raw units and axis convention have already been applied) — and 'world' is the posed CAD scene (the numbers to compare against the evaluated solid); the lean row carries the world box only. Every reference the source named appears here whether or not its file could be read: 'status' is ok, missing, unsupported, unreadable, empty, oversize or unresolved, 'reason' names the file and says what went wrong and travels at both detail levels, and a failed reference is drawn in the world as a wireframe marker at its pose. A mesh over the outline budget renders shaded without ortho outlines. Pass emit_dsl=true to get the node boxes back as .mcad KEEP-OUT envelopes in the reply's `dsl` field: one `keepout_<reference>` binding per reference, built as the union of one cube per node at that node's WORLD axis-aligned bounding box grown by clearance_mm on every side, with a comment listing the nodes it covers and the line to subtract (`part = part - keepout_board`). The box is the node's box in its WORLD pose, so a part mounted at an angle keeps the box its rotated silhouette needs and not a tight one — a keep-out is deliberately generous. nodes=[...] emits only the nodes named (path from the file root, or a bare leaf name); a name no node carries, and a node whose box is flat with clearance_mm 0, are omitted and listed in dsl_omitted. At most 200 node cubes are written: above that the call is an error asking for nodes=. This verb describes the REFERENCES; minerva_cad_get_mesh_info describes the evaluated solid.

editor_name.description: Name of the CAD editor tab (as returned by minerva_list_editors).

reference.description: Only the reference of this name (as bound in the DSL). Default: every mounted reference.

detail.description: How much of each row travels. Default 'lean': name, status, world bounding box, node count. 'full' adds the paths, the 4x4 pose, both frames of every box, the per-node boxes and the load statistics.

emit_dsl.description: Also return the node boxes as .mcad keep-out envelopes in `dsl`, one keepout_<reference> binding to subtract. Default false.

clearance_mm.description: With emit_dsl: how much air every keep-out cube keeps on each of its six sides, in millimetres. Default 0. Negative is an error.

nodes.description: With emit_dsl: emit a cube only for these nodes, each a path from the file root or a bare leaf name. Default: every node of every reference in scope, which is an error above 200 nodes.

tools.name: minerva_cad_find_holes
tools.description: Find and MEASURE the holes in a mounted reference mesh. Works in two stages: candidates are proposed by segmenting the mesh and fitting cylinders to it (no seed, no preferred axis — a hole drilled at an angle is found the same way an axis-aligned one is), then every candidate is verified against physics colliders with a ray-sampled gauge pin: rays leave the pin's axis at 24 azimuths from each of 5 stations along its length, so the verification is a SAMPLE of the wall and not a volumetric proof — a feature standing between two rays can be missed, and at a 5 mm radius 15° of arc is 1.3 mm of unsampled wall. Returns for each hole: center_mm {world, local}, axis {world, local}, dia_mm (the diameter the tessellation's circumscribed circle implies), gauge_dia_mm (the largest pin the sampled rays allow — smaller than dia_mm by the facet chord, which is why both are reported; gauge_bounded is false when no wall was met inside the search bound, and then gauge_dia_mm is 0 and gauge_dia_at_least_mm carries the floor the bound implies), inscribed_dia_mm, facets, coverage, residual_mm, through (true only when a ray passes all the way along the axis — a blind pocket looks identical to a fitter), depth_mm, verified, and source ('fit', or 'ray-grid' when the fitter found nothing and a ray-grid seed was used instead). A hole that passes through several nodes of the same file (a board's substrate, copper and mask, say) is reported ONCE, with 'nodes' listing every node it crosses and 'node' naming the first. Millimetres throughout. The first call on a newly loaded file segments it on a worker thread while the verb awaits (the app stays responsive) and builds its colliders on the main thread; both are cached until the file changes. A reply with stale: true was measured while the document changed under it — read stale_reason and call again. Pass emit_dsl=true to get the census back as .mcad in the reply's `dsl` field: one cylinder slug per radius and axis, one translate() per hole at its WORLD centre, and a comment saying what to subtract — or, with dsl_kind="post", cylinders to add at the same centres. A hole whose axis is not square to a world axis is left out and named in dsl_skipped, because a rotate() invented for it would be a guess. This is how a measured centre reaches the document without being retyped.

editor_name.description: Name of the CAD editor tab (as returned by minerva_list_editors).

reference.description: Restrict to the reference of this name (as bound in the DSL). Default: every mounted reference.

node.description: Restrict to one node inside the file, as named by minerva_cad_references.

min_dia_mm.description: Smallest hole diameter to report. Default 0.3.

max_dia_mm.description: Largest hole diameter to report. Default 30.

min_coverage.description: How much of a full turn the wall must cover to count as a hole rather than a fillet, 0..1. Default 0.6.

region_angle_deg.description: Normal-continuity angle used to segment the mesh. Raise it for a coarsely tessellated file (fewer than about 16 facets per circle). Default 25.

verified_only.description: Drop candidates the gauge could not confirm. Default false — an unverified candidate is information.

fallback.description: Fall back to a ray-grid seed when the fitter proposes nothing. Default true.

axis.description: Direction the ray-grid fallback drills along, [x, y, z] in world millimetres. Default [0, 0, 1]. The fitter itself needs no axis — this only aims the fallback grid.

pitch_mm.description: Spacing of the ray-grid fallback, in millimetres. Default 1. A hole narrower than the pitch can be missed; halving the pitch quadruples the number of rays.

emit_dsl.description: Also return the census as .mcad source in `dsl`. Default false.

dsl_kind.description: What the emitted DSL builds: 'hole' (slugs to subtract, the default) or 'post' (cylinders to add at the same centres).

dsl_clearance_mm.description: Added to every emitted RADIUS, in millimetres. Default 0 — the measured hole exactly.

dsl_depth_mm.description: Length of every emitted cylinder, in millimetres. Default 0 = three times the hole's own measured extent, so a cut is never coplanar with the face it crosses.

tools.name: minerva_cad_find_cylinders
tools.description: Like minerva_cad_find_holes but for cylindrical features of either sense: kind='concave' is bores and holes, kind='convex' is bosses, standoffs and pins, kind='any' is both. Concave candidates are verified with a gauge pin; convex ones are verified by contact with the wall: a probe straddling the fitted radius must touch it and a probe standing off that radius must touch nothing (a trimesh collider is a surface, so 'is there material inside' is not a question physics can answer). Same reported shape as find_holes, plus form ('concave'/'convex'); the same first-call segmentation (worker thread, awaited) and collider build (main thread), and the same stale: true mark when the document changed under the verb.

editor_name.description: Name of the CAD editor tab (as returned by minerva_list_editors).

reference.description: Restrict to the reference of this name.

node.description: Restrict to one node inside the file.

kind.description: Which sense of cylinder to report. Default 'any'.

min_coverage.description: Minimum fraction of a full turn the surface covers, 0..1.

region_angle_deg.description: Normal-continuity angle used to segment the mesh. Default 25.

tools.name: minerva_cad_gauge
tools.description: Put a gauge of a given size at a given place in the posed CAD world and ask whether it fits. shape='cylinder' is a pin (dia_mm + length_mm, pointing along axis), 'box' is a block (size_mm [x,y,z]), 'sphere' is a ball (dia_mm). Returns {fits, contacts[{point_mm {world, local}, node, reference, on, witness}], clearance_mm, clearance_bound_mm, clearance_bounded, measured_against}. IT MEASURES AGAINST THE EVALUATED SOLID AS WELL AS THE REFERENCES: an unscoped gauge mounts the part the document evaluates to and casts into it too, so a gauge inside your own tray floor answers fits:false with a contact whose `on` is "solid" (a solid contact has no node and no local frame — the part is in no reference's pose). A contact with witness:true is NOT a foul: a gauge buried in material thicker than itself reaches no wall, so that contact is the nearest surface of the body it is inside — do not count it as a place the gauge touched. Pass reference= to ask about ONE mounted reference instead, which leaves the solid out of the answer. Read measured_against before trusting a fit: it says how many reference colliders and whether the solid was there, with solid_reason when it was not. clearance_mm is measured for every shape — a cylinder grows radially, a sphere and a box are measured from their own surface to the nearest material. The gauge is RAY-SAMPLED, not volumetric: rays leave it at 24 azimuths from each of 5 stations along its length (plus its two ends), so 'it fits' means nothing was found on those rays — a rib or a burr between two of them can be missed. A gauge that does not fit reports where it touched, so 'why will this screw not go in' has an answer with coordinates. In open space no ray meets a wall at all: clearance_bounded is then false and the room is reported as clearance_at_least_mm, the search bound, which is a floor and not a measurement. Positions are millimetres in the posed world frame; at_mm is world.

editor_name.description: Name of the CAD editor tab (as returned by minerva_list_editors).

dia_mm.description: Diameter for cylinder and sphere gauges.

length_mm.description: Length of a cylinder gauge along its axis. Default 5.

size_mm.description: Box gauge size [x, y, z] in millimetres.

at_mm.description: Gauge centre [x, y, z] in posed world millimetres.

reference.description: Report contact points in this reference's local frame as well. Default: the reference each contact itself lies on. A contact that cannot be attributed to a reference is reported in world only, with local null and local_unavailable saying why — no reference is guessed.

tools.name: minerva_cad_check_interference
tools.description: Does the evaluated solid RUN INTO any reference mesh, and where? Returns {checked, count, point_count, pairs[{reference, node, points_mm[{world, local}], point_count, penetration_mm?, note?}], undecidable[{reference, node, reason}], sampling, casts, units:'mm'}. 'count' is the number of (reference, node) pairs the solid overlaps; 'points_mm' are the crossing points in both frames (world = the posed scene, local = that reference's own frame, the numbers you write back into the DSL); 'penetration_mm', when present, is the shorter of the two bodies' longest chords through the other: a LOWER BOUND on the overlap, not a separation depth along any contact normal (a peg through a plate runs the plate's thickness along the peg's edges and the peg's diameter along the plate's, and the shorter of the two is what comes back). 'checked': false with a 'reason' means the question could not be asked at all (no solid evaluated, or no reference mounted) — that is NOT the same answer as no interference. Every report carries source_digest, records_digest and gauge_generation — the solid, the reference poses as the gauge digests them, and the collider generation it cast against; a check that begins with a pose rewritten and the colliders not yet rebuilt rebuilds them from the current records first (colliders_rebuilt: true), so a report is never old rays framed in a new pose; and a check whose colliders were rebuilt by a newer evaluation WHILE it waited for its physics step comes back 'superseded' with 'checked': false and no stamp — the evaluation that rebuilt them is measured in its own right. This check and minerva_cad_check_fasteners share the panel's one solid collider and take it one at a time. A VERB call arriving while another check is still inside its window comes back with 'checked': false, 'busy': true and the holder's ticket and age — retry it, nothing was measured. The panel's own per-evaluation check is QUEUED instead of refused, so the newest evaluation is always the one measured and painted; a holder that has run past its window is reclaimed rather than waited on, so a check that dies never strands the panel. The test is complete for closed meshes: every edge of the solid is cast against the reference colliders, every edge of an overlapping reference triangle against a collider rebuilt from the solid this evaluation, and containment is settled by ray parity; contacts within 0.0001 mm are reported as touching, not as interference, so a part resting flush on a board is clean — including a boss whose screw pilot opens in the face that seats, where the chord over the open mouth is a contact and not a penetration. Read 'undecidable' BEFORE reading count 0 as clean: containment is decided from a probe verified inside its own body, and a node whose every probe landed in a hole, a cavity or on a shared face offered none — it is listed there with the reason and is neither cleared nor reported as interfering. Read 'sampling': it says 'none' when nothing was skipped and names the ceiling when a pathological document hit one, in which case the counts are floors. Every evaluation already carries this same report in last_eval.interference and draws the points as red crosses in the panes; call this verb to re-ask after an edit or to scope the question with reference=/node=. The reply's 'pass' is count 0 with nothing undecidable. An assembly touches itself on purpose, so pass expected_contacts:[{reference, node?, region_mm?, required_mm?}] to declare the contacts you meant: their crossings leave 'count' (and the red crosses) while the overlap stays inside what you declared, they are listed in 'expected_contacts' with the depth measured for each and counted by 'excluded_count', and one that runs deeper comes back among the pairs carrying declared_intended — a declaration can never hide a crash. That depth is a chord along an edge and not an upper bound, so an exclusion is ADVISORY: the row carries certified: false and the reply's pass is false with advisory true and a pass_reason while any declaration is excluding a pair. Every reply names the 'part' it is about; pass parts:[names] to check several DSL bindings in one call and the reply is {parts:[{part, ...}], count, failed, pass} with one report per part. REFERENCE AGAINST REFERENCE. Pass against=<other reference> (or reference="all-pairs") and this verb measures the mounted references against EACH OTHER instead of against the evaluated solid — the part-layout question that used to be read off bounding boxes by hand. The reply is {checked, mode:'reference-vs-reference', pass, required_mm, scope, pairs:[{a:{reference,node}, b:{reference,node}, min_mm, pass, point_a_mm:{world,local}, point_b_mm:{world,local}, overlap?, contact_points_mm?, penetration_mm?, expected?}], pairs_measured, pairs_considered, pairs_shown, pairs_hidden, quantization_mm, references_moved, cache, engine}, closest pairs first. It is measured node against node and never within one reference. Only the closest max_pairs candidates (200 by default) are measured, ordered by the gap between their world bounding boxes — a true LOWER BOUND on the distance — so when the reply carries unmeasured_bound_mm nothing unmeasured is closer than that number. There is no tessellation on either side, so no tessellation_tolerance_mm comes back; the only error bar is quantization_mm, the float32 step at the largest world coordinate in scope. A distance between two meshes is UNSIGNED: a pair with no air between them is reported with overlap:true and contact points that lie in the two meshes' shared BOUNDING BOX — located to that box and no finer, so a contact point can sit in air inside it, because a mesh-mesh collision names a triangle corner rather than a point of the intersection — and nothing here decides whether that is two parts resting together or one inside the other. expected_contacts works exactly as it does for the solid and matches on EITHER side of a pair. parts= is not read on this path — neither side is a DSL part. EVERY REPLY SAYS WHETHER IT IS CURRENT: source_version (the document version the evaluation on screen was of), buffer_version (the version the document is at now), evaluated_at (unix seconds) and stale. A check asked while the buffer is ahead of the evaluation — an edit that landed and has not been evaluated yet, or one still inside the debounce or with the worker — is REFUSED with checked:false and the reason rather than measuring geometry the document has moved past; call minerva_cad_await_eval and ask again.

against.description: Name a SECOND mounted reference and the measurement becomes reference-against-reference — part against part, with no involvement of the evaluated solid. Pass "all-pairs" as `reference` instead to measure every pair of mounted references. This is the off-board-layout question (does the OLED sit on the devkit, does the joystick clear the connector); it is measured from the meshes themselves, so nothing is tessellated and no tessellation tolerance is quoted. A positive distance is between SURFACES, so wherever one node's box lies inside the other's the pair is probed for containment by ray parity: a contained pair is reported as an overlap (containment: a_inside_b|b_inside_a) and never excused, and one whose containment could not be decided (an open outer mesh) withholds the pass. The verdict is graded on bound_mm — min_mm less quantization_mm — and candidate pairs beyond max_pairs whose bounding-box gap does not itself clear required_mm withhold the pass with a pass_reason.

against_node.description: Only this node inside the `against` reference — its PATH from the file root, or a bare leaf name. `node` scopes the first reference the same way. Reference-against-reference calls only.

max_pairs.description: How many node pairs one reference-against-reference call measures, closest bounding boxes first. Default 200; the reply says what it left out and how far away that was (unmeasured_bound_mm).

editor_name.description: Name of the CAD editor tab (as returned by minerva_list_editors).

parts.description: Check these named DSL bindings instead of the shape the document evaluates to, one report per part: ["bottom", "top"]. Each is evaluated as the document with that binding as its trailing expression — the DSL's own render-target rule — so a two-shell enclosure is checked as an assembly instead of one half at a time. Default: the document's own render target, whose name comes back as 'part'.

reference.description: Only this reference (by the name the DSL bound it to). Default: every mounted reference.

node.description: Only this node inside the reference — its PATH from the file root ('Assembly/Bracket/Body') for one node, or a bare leaf name for every node carrying it.

expected_contacts.description: The contacts this design MEANS to have, so the verdict can grade the rest: [{reference, node?, region_mm?, required_mm?, why?}]. `reference` is required; `node` narrows it to one node (path or leaf name) and `region_mm` ({min_mm:[x,y,z], max_mm:[x,y,z]}, world millimetres) to one PLACE on that node — naming a node alone is usually too coarse, because a board node carries both the bosses it rests on and the traces nothing may touch, and a measured contact outside the region is graded as if nothing had been declared. `required_mm` is the gap that pair must keep instead of the call's own: 0 (the default) means the surfaces may touch, a positive value grades that pair to its own bar, and a NEGATIVE value declares an intended interference fit that many millimetres deep. A declaration NEVER hides a crash: material overlap deeper than it allows (0.01 mm by default) is reported and fails anyway, an overlap with no measured depth is never excused, and every declaration comes back in `expected_contacts` with the value measured for it beside `excluded_count` (and in `expected_contacts_unmatched` when it matched nothing). `why` is free text carried into that row. An exclusion is CERTIFIED only when its evidence is: a declared overlap held inside its allowance is excused on a chord that is not an upper bound on the depth, and a region excuses the one witness point of a distance measurement without measuring the pair outside it, so both are applied ADVISORILY — the row says so (certified: false, or ungraded_outside_region) and the top-level pass is withheld with a pass_reason rather than certified; only a declared pair with a measured GAP at or above its own required_mm is a certified exclusion.

tools.name: minerva_cad_check_clearance
tools.description: How much AIR is there between the evaluated solid and each reference node, and is it enough? Returns {checked, pass, advisory, required_mm, tessellation_tolerance_mm, quantization_mm, largest_coordinate_mm, bound, pairs:[{reference, node, min_mm, bound_mm, pass, solid_point_mm, reference_point_mm:{world, local}, interference?, touching?}], solid_triangles, cache, interference_join, units:'mm'}, sorted closest-first. This is the question interference cannot answer: interference says whether two bodies touch, this says by how much they miss, which is the number you edit a wall by. The distance is EXACT for the two meshes — a minimum over triangle pairs, computed in the worker over a swept-sphere BVH, with no sampling and no pitch — and 'solid_point_mm'/'reference_point_mm' are the two points that realise it, so you know WHERE the pinch is and not only that there is one. ALWAYS quote tessellation_tolerance_mm with the number — it is what the mesh KEEPS, which is the number you asked for unless this module's finest angular step bound it first, in which case the reply states the coarser truth and keeps your request beside it as requested_tolerance_mm. 'tolerance_bounded': false means the bar is not PROVEN, and tolerance_source says why: 'sampled' is a spline face (a loft's or a sweep's flank) whose curvature was sampled on a grid and refined — a good angle, but curvature between two samples is unseen — and 'guessed' is a face the worker could not evaluate at all, left to a bounding-box guess; either way the check reports pass false and advisory true with a 'pass_reason' naming which. accept_unbounded_tolerance: true adds per-pair advisory_pass graded on min_mm against required_mm (less vertex quantization), with tolerance_waived and a waiver; it never produces a certified pass. 'references_moved': true means reference geometry changed while the check waited; pass is false, so re-ask for the current geometry. Otherwise: the solid is a B-Rep and the query measures its tessellation, whose chord step is derived from the WIDEST curvature in the part — read off a cylinder, sphere, cone or torus (which PROVES the bar) or sampled across the face where the surface has no radius to read, as on a loft's or a sweep's B-spline flanks (which estimates it and says so with tolerance_bounded false) — so on an analytic solid the stated millimetres bound every surface of it, and a curved face is measured on chords that lie inside the true surface by up to that deviation — the true clearance is at least min_mm minus it, reported per pair as bound_mm, and a pair PASSES only when bound_mm meets required_mm: the verdict and the error bar are one subtraction, so a gap that clears the requirement by less than the tolerance fails. min_mm of 0 means there is no air between the two meshes at all, and an unsigned distance cannot say whether that is contact or a crossing: such a pair comes back with touching:true, bound_mm 0 and pass false against any required_mm, and the note says whether the joined interference report calls it flush. 'interference':true is the JOINED REPORT's word and appears only for a node it actually names as crossing the solid; call minerva_cad_check_interference for where. A mesh-to-mesh distance is UNSIGNED, so a node buried inside the solid's material would measure as a positive gap on its own: the reply therefore JOINS the latest interference report for the same source, and any node it names comes back at min_mm 0 with interference:true and pass false. A node that report lists as UNDECIDABLE — its containment could not be settled — keeps its measured distance but comes back pass false with 'containment_undecidable': true and a note saying why, because an unsigned distance cannot say which side of the surface it was measured from. The same applies to a report that could not decide whether the SOLID is inside a reference: that doubt names no node, so every node of that reference carries the same flag and note. tools.name: minerva_cad_check_fasteners
tools.description: Will these screws actually go in? Pairs the evaluated solid's bores with the reference's holes, one to one, and answers four questions per screw: {reference, node, axis_source, tessellation_tolerance_mm, coaxiality:{offset_start_mm, offset_end_mm, zone_dia_mm, allowed_mm, allowed_zone_dia_mm, clearance_hole_dia_mm, clearance_source, pass}, axis_angle_deg, centre_offset_mm, path_clear (+obstructions naming the node, the point and the span — 'approach' before the mouth or 'bore' inside the engaged bore), engagement_mm, engagement_required_mm, engagement_ok, head_seat_clear, head_seat_supported, head_seat_gap_mm, head_seat_tolerance_mm, screw_tip_mm, bore_floor_mm, bottoming (+bottoming_by_mm), pass, why} in BOTH frames, plus 'unpaired' listing every solid feature and every hole that found no partner — including every cylindrical surface that is NOT a bore: only a surface that sweeps the WHOLE turn is a hole a screw can be held in — a groove five degrees short of it is open on one side, and the worker states the threshold it applied on every row so the panel applies that number rather than one of its own, and a partial one (a groove, a fillet, the end of a slot) is listed with reason 'partial cylinder (sweep N degrees)' rather than paired and graded. COAXIALITY is graded the way ISO 1101 grades it — a cylindrical zone about the hole's axis containing the bore's axis over the engaged length — against the radial slack an ISO 273:1979 MEDIUM clearance hole gives that screw (M3 -> 3.4 mm, so 0.2 mm radial). A size the medium series does not tabulate is NOT interpolated: the row comes back with coaxiality.graded false, allowed_mm null and pass null, the offsets still measured — and it does NOT fail the screw, because nobody stating the clearance is not the same as the joint being wrong. Pass clearance_hole_dia_mm to have it graded. PATH is a ray fan along the screw axis that samples the whole DISC of the shank and of the head — the axis plus concentric rings out to each radius, no two adjacent rays more than ray_spacing.radial_mm apart outwards or ray_spacing.angular_mm apart around — so a rib at mid-radius is seen and not only one across the rim; it is still sampled, not swept, so an obstruction narrower than that spacing can pass between two rays unseen, and the reply says so (rays_total counts the rays it actually placed). The SHANK fan sees the evaluated solid as well as the references, so a rib or a wall the shell grew across its own bore is caught; the two hits that are the screw arriving — the bore wall inside its own radius and span, and the boss's end face within a band of the mouth derived from that boss's measured tilt — are filtered out by name; the same shank rays then carry on down the ENGAGED bore (from the full-turn mouth to the engaged depth), where only the SOLID's own wall at the bore's radius WITH A RADIAL NORMAL may be met (a shelf or floor face ending at that radius has an axial normal and is not the wall) and anything else — a reference part at that radius (a sleeve, a pin left in the bore) included — a web, an inward rib, a floor above the stated depth — is an obstruction with span 'bore'. The same rays run on to where the screw's TIP ends (seat + length_mm): solid across the bore at or past its extent end is the FLOOR of a blind bore, and a tip that reaches it means the screw cannot seat — the row reports bottoming: true with screw_tip_mm, bore_floor_mm and bottoming_by_mm and fails, even when engagement reads as ample. The HEAD fan sees the solid as well as the references: the one solid hit it lets through is a face within head_seat_tolerance_mm of the seat plane (the solid's own seat face, or the boss top the seat plane lies in), so a shell feature standing between the head and its seat — an annular bridge outside the shank but inside the head — is reported under head_obstructions and fails head_seat_clear. head_seat_supported is CIRCUMFERENCE COVERAGE AT ONE RADIUS, not bearing area: the fraction of a single ring of rays at head_seat_radius_mm from the axis (midway between shank and head) that met material of the body the seat was read off (the reference, or the solid when seat is 'solid') within head_seat_tolerance_mm (0.05 mm along the axis — a depth tolerance, independent of the ring's lateral ray_spacing_mm) of the seat plane — an annular void inside that ring reads as 1.0, and head_seat_rule in every row says so; head_seat_gap_mm is the furthest below the seat plane the ring found a surface, so a head floating over a counterbore is reported by the millimetre. It is ADVISORY and is NOT part of `pass` — a head hanging over an edge is reported, not failed, because nothing is in its way. ORIENTATION: a row grades a hole in the REFERENCE against a bore in the SOLID, and screw.seat says which body the HEAD lands on — 'reference' for a board bolted onto bosses, 'solid' for a lid-through screw or one counterbored into a tray floor under a sandwiched board, 'offset' for a plane you place yourself. The screw travels from the hole toward the middle of its bore, so a screw arriving from below is graded the right way up without a pairs override. ENGAGEMENT is the overlap of the screw's length from the seat with the bore's FULL-CIRCUMFERENCE axial extent (bore_extent_mm) — a bore whose mouth is cut by a tilted face has thread on one side only above the low point of that trim, and bore_wall_extent_mm is where its wall reaches at its furthest azimuth — graded against engagement_min_d on the bite MINUS engagement_bound_mm (the full-turn extent is read in angular bins off a boundary sampled to a stated deflection, so it carries an error bar and a screw must clear the threshold on the shortest bite the measurement allows). When the kernel could not read a bore's own boundary at all — a parametric box was used, or an edge could not be sampled to a deflection — the row comes back engagement_certain false and engagement_ok FALSE with `why` saying the extent is not exact: an extent nobody can bound is not a pass, and it is not a verdict about the joint either (default 2.0 x d, the thread-forming-into-thermoplastic rule; use 1.0-1.5 for metal). READ axis_source on every row: 'b_rep' means the bore's axis came from the OCCT surface and is exact; 'tessellation_fit' means the kernel had no cylindrical face for it and the axis was fitted to the display mesh, carrying tessellation_tolerance_mm of chordal error. 'checked': false with a 'reason' is NOT a clean bill of health. This check and minerva_cad_check_interference share the panel's one solid collider and take it one at a time. This verb is always an agent's own question, so a call arriving while another check is still inside its window comes back with 'checked': false, 'busy': true and the holder's ticket and age — retry it, nothing was measured; the panel's per-evaluation interference check queues instead, so an evaluation is never dropped. A holder that has run past its window is reclaimed rather than waited on, so a check that dies never strands the panel. The reply carries reference_hole_index: every reference hole the check indexed, with its node, diameter, centre and `through`, numbered exactly as a `pairs` entry's reference_hole names it — a hole with no usable axis is never indexed, so this numbering is the check's own and not the order minerva_cad_find_holes reported. Obstruction lists (obstructions, head_obstructions) are collapsed to one row per (node, span): the nearest crossing, a `count` of the rays that met it, and the axial_range_mm they met it over. Every reply names the 'part' it is about; pass parts:[names] to check several DSL bindings in one call and the reply is {parts:[{part, ...}], count, failed, pass} with one report per part. The `unpaired` solid features are COLLAPSED by default to one row per diameter (grouped to 0.01 mm) and fit, as {dia_mm, count, indices, fit} — a shell has thirty-odd cylindrical surfaces no screw is going into and they are the same thirty on every call. The `indices` are exactly the solid_feature numbers a `pairs` entry names, so the override still works off the collapsed reply; a surface that was never a bore groups on its own with the sweep range that disqualified it and no index. Pass detail='full' for the features themselves, with their centres. Each screw row also carries bore_fit ('thread', 'clearance' or 'undersize'), seat_on and seat_offset_mm: overlap with a CLEARANCE bore is reported but is never engagement, because there is no material there for the thread to hold. EVERY REPLY SAYS WHETHER IT IS CURRENT: source_version (the document version the evaluation on screen was of), buffer_version (the version the document is at now), evaluated_at (unix seconds) and stale. A check asked while the buffer is ahead of the evaluation — an edit that landed and has not been evaluated yet, or one still inside the debounce or with the worker — is REFUSED with checked:false and the reason rather than measuring geometry the document has moved past; call minerva_cad_await_eval and ask again.
